theme: Dark Theme (ARCHETYPE 2: THE PERFORMANCE PRO) - Tactical Gym Aesthetic

headings.usage: Massive oversized numeric typography for live stats and high-impact moments. Maximum text-6xl for hero, text-4xl for dashboard widgets.

body.usage: Geometric sans with increased tracking for legibility in dense lists and history logs.

rules: Use extremely high contrast for critical data.
Never use pure black or pure grey without a slight tint.
Status badges with color coding (Green, Red, Yellow) are absolutely critical for the history calendar.

surfaces.tactical_look: Replace soft shadows with 1px solid strokes (border-white/10) or 2px Inner Glow highlights.
surfaces.headers: Use Solid Background with a hard bottom border (#27272A). NEVER use transparent backgrounds over content.
surfaces.employee_clock_button: Use a massive, tactile variant of Neumorphism. It should feel like pushing a physical, heavy machine button. High contrast, sharp inner edges.

borders.grid_technical: Expose the skeleton. Data-heavy dashboards (Admin) should use border-r border-b border-border/40 to create a technical/tactical look.

component_rules.general: Use pure HTML/Tailwind for custom layouts (like the giant employee punch-in dashboard). Use Shadcn/UI primitives for tables, forms, and dialogs in the Admin dashboard.
component_rules.buttons: Pill-shaped or sharp rectangular buttons. NEVER use HTML <select>, always Shadcn dropdowns.
component_rules.inputs: Shadcn input and select components exclusively. Do not use generic native elements.
component_rules.calendar: Admin and Employee history require a Calendar grid. MUST use Shadcn calendar component. Days must show the green/red/yellow status dots.
component_rules.toast: Use `sonner` for toast notifications (e.g., successful punch-in/out, saved admin settings). Located in /app/frontend/src/components/ui/sonner.jsx.

grids_layouts.employee_dashboard: Mobile-first priority. Full-height layout where the 'Clock In/Out' interaction takes up 60%+ of the viewport height. Massive hit targets.
grids_layouts.admin_dashboard: High Density Grid (MODE B). Tight gaps (gap-4). Every pixel utilized. col-span-3 for main user lists, col-span-1 for summary widgets.
grids_layouts.spacing: Generous Spacing Philosophy. Use p-6 or p-8 inside cards. Containers with borders MUST have internal padding.

motion.clock_in_button: Tactical feedback: Heavy scale-down (transform: scale(0.95)) on press with a swift release. It must feel 'alive' and responsive to physical effort.
motion.hover_states: ALWAYS explicitly set text color on hover (e.g., hover:bg-slate-900 hover:text-white). Focus states must have HIGHER contrast.
motion.transitions: Use specific properties (transition: transform 0.2s ease, opacity 0.2s ease). DO NOT use `transition: all` as it breaks transforms.

accessibility.contrast: Minimum 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text. Prefer APCA contrast rules.
accessibility.testing: All interactive and key informational elements MUST include a `data-testid` attribute (kebab-case, role-based). Examples: `data-testid="clock-in-button"`, `data-testid="admin-save-coords-button"`.

media.strategy: Atmospheric, dark, cinematic fitness imagery to reinforce the tactical aesthetic.

hero_bg.description: Dark and atmospheric gym interior showcasing weights with dramatic lighting.
hero_bg.usage: Use as an opacity-reduced background (max 30% opacity, bg-black/70 overlay) for the login screen or massive employee dashboard to add depth without distracting from the clock-in button.

admin_bg.description: Dark, atmospheric gym with mirrored weightlifting machines and neon lighting.
admin_bg.usage: Use as a subtle hero header graphic in the admin settings.

instructions_to_main_agent: Design a mobile-first PWA for Gym Employees (Fichaje/Clock-in).
Focus on the 'Elite Athleticism & Precision' archetype. Use deep blacks and sharp borders.
Implement the Employee dashboard with a massive, satisfying clock-in button.
Implement the Admin Dashboard using high-density grid layouts for user CRUD and coordinate settings.
CRITICAL: The Monthly Calendar history MUST display colored indicators based on punch type: Green (#10B981) for Manual, Red (#EF4444) for Auto-closed, Yellow (#F59E0B) for Admin-edited.
Ensure all Shadcn components (calendar, select, table) conform to the dark tactical theme.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. In frontend design, this creates what users call the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
Dark colors look good when used independently without gradients. DO NOT use dark colors as gradients.
Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Use glass-morphism effects with backdrop filters (12-24px blur).
You MUST NOT apply universal transition. Eg: `transition: all`. This results in breaking transforms. Always add transitions for specific interactive elements like button, input excluding transforms.
You MUST NOT center align the app container, ie do not add `.App { text-align: center; }` in the css file. This disrupts the human natural reading flow of text.
Always use modern button styles like pill-shaped, or sharp button with interaction animations & color relevant to the app style.
NEVER: use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡🔮🎯 etc for icons.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions, parallax effects, and entrance animations. Static = dead.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap.
Subtle grain textures, noise overlays, custom cursors, selection states, and loading animations: separates good from extraordinary.
Main agent relies on these image URLs. Missing categories (especially sponsor logos) = main agent will use placeholder text which is FORBIDDEN.
Prioritize using pre-existing components from src/components/ui when applicable.
Create new components that match the style and conventions of existing components when needed.
Examine existing components to understand the project's component patterns before creating new ones.
